headline: Chips Lead a Broad Friday Rally as Software Slumps and Geopolitics Reshape the Energy Trade
body_html:
Stocks closed out the week on a constructive note Friday, with advancers outnumbering decliners by nearly two to one across the 545-name universe — 348 issues higher versus 195 lower. Semiconductors were the unmistakable engine of the session, posting a group gain of 2.44%, as investors rotated into hardware-linked names while pulling back from enterprise software. Homebuilders added 1.31% and materials climbed 1.09%, suggesting the bid was broad enough to extend well beyond pure technology.

The rotation away from software was pointed. The security and identity subsectors bore the brunt of selling, with the broader software group off 0.82% on the day. Energy also slipped 0.41%, weighed down by a roughly 2% drop in crude prices after diplomatic signals between Washington and Tehran opened the possibility of a negotiated pause in regional hostilities — a development that removed some of the geopolitical risk premium embedded in oil.

MaxLinear stood out as the session's defining mover, surging 10.0% to top the leaderboard, with Veeco Instruments and Credo Technology adding 9.28% and 7.65% respectively to reinforce the semiconductor theme. On the other side of the ledger, Zscaler shed more than 10%, the steepest single-name decline, as the cybersecurity cohort absorbed concentrated pressure. Heading into month-end, the divergence between silicon and software bears watching.

briefs.headline: MaxLinear Tops the Board With a 10% Surge
briefs.body: MaxLinear finished as Friday's standout performer, jumping exactly 10.0% to lead the entire universe. Connectivity and semiconductor-equipment names rode the same current, with Veeco Instruments up 9.28% and Credo Technology gaining 7.65%, underscoring a concentrated appetite for chip-chain exposure into the weekend.

briefs.headline: Zscaler Drops More Than 10% in Sharpest Single-Stock Decline
briefs.body: Zscaler fell 10.06% — the session's deepest percentage loss — dragging the cybersecurity corner of the software market lower alongside it. Qualys shed 5.75% and Okta lost 5.54%, making software-security the most conspicuous pocket of selling pressure on an otherwise broadly positive Friday.

briefs.headline: Oil Retreats as U.S.-Iran Diplomatic Signals Emerge
briefs.body: Crude prices declined roughly 2% after reports indicated the United States and Iran were exploring a potential off-ramp from the ongoing regional conflict, with Tehran proposing a seven-day framework to halt fighting. The move pressured the energy sector, which closed down 0.41%, even as Iran's foreign minister signaled the next step rests with Washington.

briefs.headline: Microsoft's Copilot Revamp Draws Investor Enthusiasm
briefs.body: Microsoft received a notable lift after unveiling a significant overhaul of its Copilot artificial-intelligence assistant, with observers noting the redesign addressed widely cited shortcomings in the product. The positive market reception highlighted continued investor sensitivity to credible AI product iteration from large platform companies.

briefs.headline: Treasury Yields Near Multi-Decade Highs Attract Bond Buyers
briefs.body: The 10-year Treasury yield has climbed to levels not seen in nineteen years, a move that is beginning to attract a contingent of investors who view current rates as a generational buying opportunity in fixed income. The dynamic adds a layer of cross-asset complexity for equity allocators navigating month-end positioning.

briefs.headline: Paramount-WBD Merger Terms Spark Hollywood Skepticism
briefs.body: Details emerged Friday outlining the specific commitments Paramount made to the entertainment industry in order to advance its combination with Warner Bros. Discovery, yet portions of the creative community remained unconvinced the pledges would be honored in practice. The deal continues to draw scrutiny over its long-term structural implications for the studio landscape.
